issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no hard-coded answers, and test labels are not used. The test molecules are only passed to predict.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The edit averages 5 seeded two-stage XGB fits (seed*10+k), so randomness still comes from the seed argument. random_state was moved out of params, so it is not passed twice.

Recomputed z = (0.3655 - 0.365) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1 + 1/2)) = 0.0005 / 0.00453 ≈ 0.11. This agrees with the harness value of 0.112; the small gap comes from rounding in the displayed means. The change is well within noise, so 'reject' is correct.

Side note: the 5-model ensemble makes the XGB part about 5 times as expensive and adds code for no measurable gain. That goes against 'simpler is better'. It is worth checking the job time against the 10-minute limit if this idea is tried again.
